children: U.S. grain futures on the Chicago Board of Trade rallied Monday after initial U.S.-China trade talks were described as positive by both sides, raising hopes that the planned meeting between President Trump and China's Xi Jinping will include Chinese commitments to buy more U.S. agricultural products.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent said discussions between the two sides had been "very successful," and Li Chenggang, the top Chinese trade negotiator, said the talks were conducted in a good atmosphere.

Markets will be closely watching the Trump-Xi meeting for any signs of agricultural purchases by the Chinese government, which the Trump administration has said promised to buy at least $17B of farm exports.
China has separately pledged to buy 25M tons/year of U.S. soybeans, meaning any additional commitments likely would include grains such as wheat or corn.

"U.S. grains should benefit from this week's meeting as U.S. President Trump looks for a diplomatic win ahead of the midterms," AgResource said in a note. "There is also high hope that China will drop its 10% tariff on U.S. soybeans and grain."

Black Sea disruptions also supported agriculture prices, with Russian forces striking two bulk carriers near Odessa and port infrastructure at Izmail, while the Moscow Oil Refinery was hit in drone attacks that were called the largest overnight Ukrainian barrage this year.
